title: Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC): ASHA Practice Portal
population: People who use or may benefit from AAC across ages and diagnoses.
summary: Organizes assessment, multimodal communication, feature matching, partner support and intervention considerations, with linked research and evidence summaries.
limitations: Living clinical guidance synthesizes heterogeneous evidence and does not rank products or replace individualized assessment. The year is the review/access year, not a fixed publication year.
review_basis: Targeted review of the published abstract, official guidance or available article text; no formal risk-of-bias assessment.

title: Augmentative and Alternative Communication Generative Language Intervention: A Randomized Controlled Trial
population: 40 preschool children requiring AAC, with relatively intact receptive language, in intervention, control or both conditions.
summary: A play-based 28-session AAC-GLI program produced better growth in aided expressive grammar than a caregiver workshop alone. The study extends AAC outcomes beyond requesting and single-word vocabulary.
limitations: Small sample, pandemic-related enrollment and attrition, and restricted receptive-language profile limit generalization. Outcomes used a specialized aided-grammar measure rather than broad life-participation measures.
conditions: Cerebral palsy; Childhood apraxia of speech
review_basis: Targeted review of the published abstract, official guidance or available article text; no formal risk-of-bias assessment.

title: Caregiving in the US 2025
population: US family caregivers
summary: Reports the scale and complexity of family caregiving, including financial, employment, and health-related experiences. Highlights caregiver support as a cross-condition resource need.
limitations: Self-reported survey estimates; changes in definitions and coverage, including attention to paid family caregivers, should be examined before comparing editions or subgroups.
review_basis: Publisher, author-hosted, or PubMed record/abstract; targeted source review

title: Generative Language Intervention for Young Children With Down Syndrome Using Augmentative and Alternative Communication: A Randomized Controlled Trial
population: Young children with Down syndrome who received AAC devices; families in both groups received workshops.
summary: Children receiving four months of twice-weekly play-based AAC Generative Language Intervention showed stronger aided expressive-grammar performance than a device-and-workshop comparison condition.
limitations: Pandemic-related recruitment and attrition affected the study. The specific intervention and grammar measure should not be generalized to every language outcome or every child with Down syndrome.
review_basis: Targeted review of the published abstract, official guidance or available article text; no formal risk-of-bias assessment.

title: Listen up! perspectives of people of color who use augmentative and alternative communication in the United States
population: Seven AAC users of color in the United States, participating over eight weeks.
summary: Participants described identity, AAC system features, provider experiences and racial inequities, highlighting the need for culturally and linguistically responsive services and technology.
limitations: Small qualitative sample provides depth rather than prevalence estimates or representation of all racial, cultural and language communities. Published online in 2024; journal issue dated 2025.
review_basis: Targeted review of the published abstract, official guidance or available article text; no formal risk-of-bias assessment.

title: What are we targeting when we support inclusive education for autistic students? A systematic review of 233 empirical studies and call for community partnerships
population: Autistic students in mainstream schooling; 233 experimental studies
summary: Finds considerable variation in inclusion measures and frequent focus on students' social behaviors. Lived-experience consultation highlights the importance of environmental adaptation and participation when interpreting these outcomes.
limitations: A map of interventions and outcome choices, not a ranking of school programs. Many included studies did not measure implementation adequately.
review_basis: Published abstract and lay abstract.

title: An Accurate and Rapidly Calibrating Speech Neuroprosthesis
population: One participant with ALS and severe dysarthria.
summary: An intracortical system decoded attempted speech with an extensive vocabulary after relatively limited calibration, demonstrating a promising communication research direction.
limitations: Single participant, invasive implantation, substantial research support and protocol-specific performance. It does not establish broad safety, effectiveness, affordability or routine availability.
review_basis: Targeted review of the published abstract, official guidance or available article text; no formal risk-of-bias assessment.

title: Communication Bill of Rights, 3rd Edition
population: Children and adults with significant communication support needs.
summary: Frames communication as participation, choice, dignity, access to information and reliable support. Useful for reviewing directory resources and services from the perspective of the person communicating.
limitations: A normative framework, not an intervention-effectiveness study or a statement of jurisdiction-specific legal entitlements.
review_basis: Targeted review of the published abstract, official guidance or available article text; no formal risk-of-bias assessment.

title: Developing the self-determination of children and young people with intellectual disabilities in schools: A systematic review of the literature
population: School-aged students with intellectual disabilities; 18 studies
summary: Maps school practices for self-determination and notes limited student involvement in deciding how supports are individualized. Supports connecting education, transition and supported decision-making resources.
limitations: Evidence concentrates on US transition-aged students with mild to moderate intellectual disabilities. Generalization to younger students and people with more extensive support needs is limited.
review_basis: Published abstract.

title: From assistive to inclusive? A systematic review of the uses and effects of technology to support people with pervasive support needs
population: People with profound intellectual and multiple disabilities; 64 studies
summary: Finds that studied technologies largely address individual development and self-determination. Mainstream and universal-design technologies receive less research attention, suggesting a gap in how inclusion is evaluated.
limitations: A heterogeneous narrative synthesis; it does not establish equivalent effectiveness for all technologies or populations.
review_basis: Published abstract.

title: Theories, models and frameworks to understand barriers to the provision of mobility-assistive technologies: a scoping review
population: 18 articles about access to mobility-assistive technology
summary: Identifies service provision, costs, policy, environment and individual factors as interacting influences on access. Supports including assessment, training, repair and funding alongside device providers.
limitations: Restricted to English-language studies using a theory, model or framework. The resulting model is a synthesis, not a trial proving that one service model works best.
review_basis: Published abstract and methods summary.

title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
population: Web content and interface users, including people with disabilities
summary: Provides testable accessibility criteria for web content, including keyboard interaction, focus visibility, target size and accessible forms. A practical foundation for maintaining a usable resource directory.
limitations: A technical standard, not evidence that this site conforms. Automated checks alone cannot establish accessibility, and individual needs can extend beyond conformance criteria.
review_basis: Official W3C Recommendation; 2024 revision of the 2023 recommendation.

title: Accessibility by Design in Clinical Research Toolkit
population: Clinical researchers, sponsors, ethics committees, and disabled participants
summary: Offers practical considerations for including people with disabilities throughout clinical research and was developed with disabled people, caregivers, and research stakeholders.
limitations: Guidance rather than a trial of effectiveness. The landing page dates initial release to 2023 and links an updated version dated April 2024; implementation depends on study context.
review_basis: Publisher, author-hosted, or PubMed record/abstract; targeted source review

title: Psychosocial Interventions and Support Groups for Siblings of Individuals with Neurodevelopmental Conditions: A Mixed Methods Systematic Review of Sibling Self-reported Mental Health and Wellbeing Outcomes
population: Siblings of people with neurodevelopmental conditions; 24 intervention studies
summary: Reports some improvements in knowledge, self-esteem and adjustment, with small favorable differences in some controlled comparisons. Supports making sibling-specific support visible in the directory.
limitations: Programs, outcome measures and family circumstances varied. The review does not establish that a particular support-group model will benefit every sibling.
review_basis: Published abstract; online publication 2022, journal issue 2023.

title: Excluding People With Disabilities From Clinical Research: Eligibility Criteria Lack Clarity And Justification
population: 97 interventional research protocols in four therapeutic areas
summary: Found broad investigator discretion and limited documented justification for disability-related exclusions. Calls for clearer eligibility criteria and accessible study design.
limitations: Protocol text does not establish actual enrollment or accommodation practices; four therapeutic areas and a selected protocol sample limit generalization.
review_basis: Publisher, author-hosted, or PubMed record/abstract; targeted source review

title: Global report on health equity for persons with disabilities
type: WHO global evidence and policy report
population: Persons with disabilities across countries and health systems
summary: Synthesizes disability-related health inequities and actions for inclusive health systems. Supports treating general disability access as a distinct cross-cutting area in the directory.
limitations: Global synthesis with differences in underlying country data; not an individualized clinical guideline or a current estimate for every jurisdiction.
review_basis: Publisher, author-hosted, or PubMed record/abstract; targeted source review

title: Respite Care for Children with Complex Care Needs: A Literature Review
population: Parents using respite services for children with complex care needs
summary: Examines parental experiences of respite services and highlights the need to understand service quality and the perspectives of children and siblings. Useful for separating respite navigation from general caregiver information.
limitations: Qualitative service-experience evidence does not provide a pooled causal estimate of respite benefits. Children's and siblings' perspectives remain a research gap.
review_basis: Indexed publication abstract and publisher bibliographic metadata; online 2021, issue 2022.

title: Physicians' Perceptions Of People With Disability And Their Health Care
population: 714 practicing US physicians
summary: Documents negative disability-related perceptions and limited confidence in equitable care among many surveyed physicians. Supports attention to provider attitudes, training, and accessible services.
limitations: Self-reported attitudes in a physician sample; the survey cannot establish that attitudes caused particular patient outcomes.
review_basis: Publisher, author-hosted, or PubMed record/abstract; targeted source review

title: Pediatric Feeding Disorder: Consensus Definition and Conceptual Framework
population: Children with feeding difficulties
summary: Frames pediatric feeding problems across medical, nutritional, feeding-skill and psychosocial domains. This supports organizing feeding resources by the kind of support needed rather than by equipment alone.
limitations: A consensus classification framework, not a comparative trial of treatments. Diagnosis and care require individualized assessment.
review_basis: Published abstract and author-institution bibliographic record; full text retrieval was blocked.

title: Effect of Genetic Diagnosis on Patients with Previously Undiagnosed Disease
population: 382 patients completing evaluation in the US Undiagnosed Diseases Network
summary: Reports diagnoses in 35% of evaluated participants and describes changes in treatment recommendations, further testing, and genetic counseling after diagnosis.
limitations: Highly selected referrals with challenging undiagnosed conditions; diagnostic yield does not predict an individual person's chance of diagnosis or apply to all clinical settings.
review_basis: Publisher, author-hosted, or PubMed record/abstract; targeted source review

title: Incorporating a Peer-Mediated Approach Into Speech-Generating Device Intervention: Effects on Communication of Preschoolers With Autism Spectrum Disorder
type: Randomized controlled trial with repeated measures
population: 45 nonspeaking or minimally speaking autistic preschoolers and 95 peers without disabilities.
summary: Training peers to use the same speech-generating system during preschool activities improved communication rates and reciprocity relative to untrained-peer comparison; gains generalized and were maintained within the study.
limitations: A specific preschool program and technology were studied. Findings do not compare all AAC systems or establish long-term outcomes across later schooling.
review_basis: Targeted review of the published abstract, official guidance or available article text; no formal risk-of-bias assessment.

title: Supporting the Health Care Transition From Adolescence to Adulthood in the Medical Home
population: Adolescents and young adults, including those with special healthcare needs
summary: Presents a structured approach to transition planning, transfer, and integration into adult care, including systems, training, payment, and research recommendations.
limitations: Professional guidance rather than an intervention trial. A foundational 2018 report; local implementation and subsequent updates need consideration.
review_basis: Publisher, author-hosted, or PubMed record/abstract; targeted source review

title: Eye gaze performance for children with severe physical impairments using gaze-based assistive technology: A longitudinal study
population: 10 children aged 1-15 years with severe physical impairments and no speaking ability.
summary: Eye-gaze performance improved over a prolonged period of practice and support. The study suggests that brief initial device trials can miss skills that develop with sustained opportunities.
limitations: Small heterogeneous sample without a randomized control group. Computer targeting performance is not equivalent to functional language, participation or a guarantee of eye-gaze suitability.
review_basis: Targeted review of the published abstract, official guidance or available article text; no formal risk-of-bias assessment.

title: The Development and Evaluation of an Online Healthcare Toolkit for Autistic Adults and their Primary Care Providers
type: Community-based participatory development and single-arm pre/post evaluation
population: Autistic adults and primary care providers
summary: Describes co-development of an accommodation report and healthcare toolkit with autistic people. Evaluation reported fewer barriers and improvements in some self-reported care measures.
limitations: Short follow-up and an uncontrolled pre/post design limit causal claims; suitability and accessibility still need individual assessment.
review_basis: Publisher, author-hosted, or PubMed record/abstract; targeted source review

title: The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship
population: Scientific data and digital research objects
summary: Defines principles for findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reuse that help explain why consistent metadata and provenance are useful in resource and registry catalogs.
limitations: A principles paper rather than an empirical demonstration. FAIR accessibility can include controlled access; it does not require publishing sensitive participant data openly.
review_basis: Publisher, author-hosted, or PubMed record/abstract; targeted source review

title: Communication interventions for minimally verbal children with autism: a sequential multiple assignment randomized trial
population: 61 minimally verbal autistic children aged 5-8 years.
summary: Beginning a blended developmental and behavioral intervention with a speech-generating device favored spontaneous communicative utterances, novel words and comments compared with beginning without the device.
limitations: The tested treatment was a multicomponent intervention, not the device alone. Sample size and follow-up limit generalization to other ages, profiles and approaches.
review_basis: Targeted review of the published abstract, official guidance or available article text; no formal risk-of-bias assessment.

title: Effect of a multi-level intervention on nurse-patient communication in the intensive care unit: results of the SPEACS trial
population: 89 awake, responsive, intubated patients unable to speak and 30 nurses in two intensive-care units.
summary: Communication training, tools and speech-language-pathology consultation supported more successful pain communication, greater AAC use and lower reported communication difficulty. Some improvements differed between units.
limitations: Nonrandomized sequential cohorts and two units at one center limit causal inference and generalizability. It does not show uniform improvement in every measured outcome.
review_basis: Targeted review of the published abstract, official guidance or available article text; no formal risk-of-bias assessment.

title: Effect of an enhanced medical home on serious illness and cost of care among high-risk children with chronic illness: a randomized clinical trial
population: 201 high-risk children with chronic illness at one Houston clinic
summary: An enhanced medical home combining primary and specialty care reduced serious illness and healthcare utilization compared with usual care in the studied population.
limitations: Single center, selected high-risk population, small clinician group, and early stopping limit generalizability. Results do not establish that every care-coordination model has the same effect.
review_basis: Publisher, author-hosted, or PubMed record/abstract; targeted source review

title: Launching PCORnet, a national patient-centered clinical research network
population: US clinical data networks and patient-powered research networks
summary: Explains the initial design of a national network combining electronic health data and patient partnership for comparative effectiveness research.
limitations: Describes the network at launch, not its present structure or measured effectiveness; use the current PCORnet website for operational information.
review_basis: Publisher, author-hosted, or PubMed record/abstract; targeted source review

title: Patient- and family-centered care coordination: a framework for integrating care for children and youth across multiple systems
population: Children and youth needing coordinated care across health and community systems
summary: Defines a family-centered approach connecting primary, specialty, educational, and community services. Useful for organizing care-coordination and navigation resources.
limitations: A policy framework rather than a causal evaluation. Foundational guidance must be adapted to contemporary local services and funding.
review_basis: Publisher, author-hosted, or PubMed record/abstract; targeted source review

title: Randomized comparison of augmented and nonaugmented language interventions for toddlers with developmental delays and their parents
population: 68 toddlers with developmental delays and fewer than 10 spoken words; 62 completed intervention.
summary: Parent-coached augmented-input and augmented-output conditions produced larger vocabulary outcomes than the spoken-only condition. The study did not support withholding AAC out of concern that it would inhibit speech.
limitations: Relatively small and selected toddler sample; outcomes came from intervention sessions and target vocabulary. It does not establish that every AAC system or intervention produces the same results.
review_basis: Targeted review of the published abstract, official guidance or available article text; no formal risk-of-bias assessment.

title: Training volunteers as conversation partners using "Supported Conversation for Adults with Aphasia" (SCA): a controlled trial
population: Adults with aphasia interacting with trained or comparison-group volunteer conversation partners.
summary: Foundational trial testing whether training conversation partners helps reveal and support the communicative competence of adults with aphasia. It supports treating partner skills as an intervention target.
limitations: Volunteer-partner context and a specific training approach limit transfer to all family, health-care or device-based situations; it is not a comparison of AAC technologies.
review_basis: Targeted review of the published abstract, official guidance or available article text; no formal risk-of-bias assessment.

title: FDA: Real-World Data: Assessing Registries to Support Regulatory Decision-Making for Drug and Biological Products
population: Patient organizations, registry planners, researchers and community partners.
summary: Considerations for selecting or designing a registry intended to support regulatory decisions about drug safety or effectiveness. Useful when a patient organization wants to understand why data collection requires an explicit research purpose.
limitations: Does not select a vendor or recommend particular study designs or statistical analysis methods. Regulatory suitability must be assessed for the proposed use.
review_basis: Targeted reading of official guidance or available provider documentation; no formal risk-of-bias assessment.

title: NCATS RaDaR: Create Your Registry Plan
population: Patient organizations, registry planners, researchers and community partners.
summary: A planning module for defining a registry’s goals and organizing its development before selecting software. Includes a planning template for community and research stakeholders.
limitations: Planning support does not establish ethics approval, technical capability or a sustainable operating budget.
year_note: 2026 is the access year; this is a living web resource.
review_basis: Targeted reading of official guidance or available provider documentation; no formal risk-of-bias assessment.

title: PCORI Foundational Expectations for Partnerships in Research
population: Patient organizations, registry planners, researchers and community partners.
summary: A framework for setting expectations when patients, caregivers and other partners contribute to research. Useful for structuring roles and relationships in patient-led projects.
limitations: Guidance is a starting point for partnership design, not evidence that a particular project is inclusive or effective.
year_note: 2026 is the access year; consult the page for framework versions.
review_basis: Targeted reading of official guidance or available provider documentation; no formal risk-of-bias assessment.

title: Got Transition: Six Core Elements of Health Care Transition
population: Patient organizations, registry planners, researchers and community partners.
summary: A structured approach to preparing for and completing healthcare transition, with tools for pediatric, adult and lifespan practices. Complements family-facing readiness and planning materials.
limitations: Implementation tools do not themselves arrange an adult provider, insurance coverage or services. Adaptation and clinical coordination are still required.
year_note: 2026 is the access year. Current program activity is documented separately from the age of its tools.
review_basis: Targeted reading of official guidance or available provider documentation; no formal risk-of-bias assessment.
